properties.name: Treble Cone
properties.takeoff_description: pub corner 500m before TC ski field. Possible to take off towards NE and SE.
properties.flight_rules:
All open and uncontrolled airspace, all the freedom you may wish for XC.
Share the space and beware of speedgliders and acro gliders.
All about NZ airspace: http://www.nzairspace.appspot.com/
properties.going_there:
Wanaka, suivre Treble Cone ski field.
When the gate is open, you can go up by car. 
Shuttle bus also available but places may be limited (5NZD as of 2011).

When parking the car at landing site, ALWAYS park it on the RIGHT side of the road (north side) at the fence. The other side is dedicated to landings. Do not park there!
properties.comments:
Contact local pilots

wait for more info
properties.weather: Strong W winds.

landing.landing_description:
At start of the road up to the ski field.
Please beware of very prickly bushes and high wire fences around the narrow landing strip.
Wind at landing can change its direction very abruptly. Observe well the windsock while still at altitude.

properties.name: Dills Hill
properties.takeoff_description:
Site Rating:
  PG: P.G.2
  HG: Novice

Takeoff height is 700ft ASL and 400ft above the landing paddock.
properties.flight_rules:
This site is located within TMA C with a flight ceiling of 4,500 ft ASL. Kaipara flats air field almost directly in front to the North East is a parachute drop zone with a 3 nautical mile no flying restriction. Both Kaipara flats and North Shore air fields need to be advised of your presence here prior to flying.

If you expect to go cross country heading in a south westerly i.e. anything on the southern side of Woodcock Rd linking through to Araparera remember the flight ceiling is 3,500 ft ASL.
properties.going_there: Located West of Warkworth you reach the site by driving North along State Highway 1 to Warkworth. As you enter the township of Warkworth take the first turn left (Woodcocks Rd) and follow this road for 10km to a railway crossing. Continue up the hill for about 1.5km until you reach the top at a sharp right hand bend with a pull over area and gate to a pine forest on the left. On the right there is a clay dry weather only track leading to the takeoff. Go through 2 more gates up to the trig and then you are in the launch area.
properties.comments: This site often closes for lambing during September.
properties.weather:
Be careful of scratching low down amongst the spines if the wind is very cross.

There is a good top landing in the paddock to the left of takeoff however do not go behind the crest on the top landing as this can be expensive in aluminium and pride. Although there are a number of possible landing paddocks take care to thoroughly scrutinise these on foot beforehand as some have little streams and gullies running through them plus a few bulls! If the wind is off to the east - southeast landing can be turbulent.

properties.name: Paeroa Range
properties.takeoff_description: Awesome high site, that just seems to draw thermals to it.
properties.flight_rules: Airspace restrictions above.
properties.going_there: You cannot independently visit this site.  There are locked gates, per-person fees, and other special requirements.  Please contact your local club.

properties.name: Kaimai
properties.going_there: Kaimais is private property and a sensitive site, with access restrictions and locked gates.  You MUST approach a keyholder.  You cannot independently visit this site.  Any poor behaviour or stupid antics on Kaimai will be dealt with by other members on site, or else very shortly after.

properties.name: Queenstown - Crown Terrace
properties.takeoff_description:
West wind , need quite a bit for soaring

rather small but not much too difficult
properties.going_there: road from Queenstown to Wanaka, at the top of the zig zag, 100 m above lookout. go through the gate on your right.
properties.weather: watch white caps on the lake give you good indication of wind coming. white caps: DON T FLY! too strong.

properties.name: Allendale
properties.takeoff_description:
Summit road  - 1 km south of the radar (big green ball at the summit)
Lower takeoff is best in light winds.
On the top takeoff keep the 'runway' clear for top landings.
properties.flight_rules: Dont fly over 3500 fts AMSL
properties.going_there: Follow the Summit road, 6 or 7 kms south of the Sign of the Kiwi
properties.comments:
Contact local pilots.
It's a good site if Taylors Mistake has too little wind but good direction.
Closed during lambing season.

landing.landing_description:
By the living Spring road turn off. Private property, farm beside. Thank the guy. Watch the power line all around the field. plus its a bit slopy. Bit technical.
Better to do a slope landing close to the top or a top landing beside the rock pile with a wind sock on it.
Best hang gliding landing is on the north of the Teddington straights.  Power lines run along the road.
Another great place to land is in the paddock beside the Wheatsheif Tavern in Teddington.

properties.name: Barnett Park
properties.takeoff_description: summit road -
properties.flight_rules: Dont fly over 3500 fts AMSL
properties.going_there: Summit Road. 500 m East from the Mt Pleasant access road.
properties.comments:
Contact local pilots.
Watch for the High Tension Power Lines.
properties.weather: watch for white caps on the Sea to check wind velocity.

landing.landing_description: by Barnett Park. look on the map.

properties.name: Taylors Mistake
properties.takeoff_description: 2km from Evans Pass on the road to Godley Head.
properties.flight_rules: Dont fly over 3500 fts AMSL
properties.going_there: Through Sumner towards Lyttleton, turn left at Evans Pass, drive 2 kilometers.
properties.comments: Very nice looking and smooth wind site.
properties.weather: Watch for white caps on the sea to check wind velocity.

landing.landing_description: Taylors mistake beach, grass field behind car park.

properties.name: Moirs Hill
properties.takeoff_description:
Site Rating:
  PG: P.G.2
  HG: Intermediate

Takeoff is at 1,050ft ASL, 800ft above the landing paddock.
properties.flight_rules:
Located in TMA C, flight ceiling immediately above launch is 3,500ft ASL, rising to 4,500ft as soon as you cross Woodcocks Rd, heading in a north or north easterly direction. Heading south across the valley takes you into North Shore airfield training space with a continued flight ceiling of 3,500ft. Every time this site is flown both North Shore airfield and Kaipara Flats airfield should be advised of your presence.

As Kaipara Flats airfield is located directly north of this site (usually immediately downwind) and this airfield is used as a parachute drop zone, there is a no flying restriction within a 3 nautical mile radius of the airfield. This restriction can be reduced on occasions if the airfield is not being used by obtaining their express consent to cut through the south eastern sector, no closer that 2 nautical miles from the airfield.
properties.going_there: Access to the site is 6km north of the Puhoi turn off on State Highway 1. Turn left into Moirs Hill Rd, adjacent to the rest area at the end of Windy Ridge. Follow this gravel road to the end and park beside the transmitter tower. Access from this point is by foot through the left hand gate, following the track to the end (15 mn).
properties.comments: Particular care should be taken to ensure all gates are closed as the farmer has concerns as to his stock being released into the Department of Conservation reserve and ferral goats from the reserve getting into his property. The availability of the landing paddock should be checked around lambing and haymaking times. Hay paddocks are usually shut off from stock from Nov through to Jan.

landing.landing_description:
Landing requires careful consideration being in a valley with the wind usually coming from one end or the other. An aircraft type landing circuit approach is strongly recommended to determine the wind direction in the bottom of the valley (often different from the wind on launch).

Top landing on takeoff is possible although very tight for hang gliders and often quite thermic posing difficulty for paragliders. An alternative top landing is available to the north east of the transmitter tower requiring a minimum of 600ft above takeoff before making an approach.

Top landing at any point should only be attempted by those experienced in top landing.

properties.name: Maioro
properties.takeoff_description:
Site Rating:
  PG: P.G.2
  HG: Novice/Intermediate
properties.going_there: Access through the farm property is restricted. Access to the site is via Karioitahi with an approximately 7km drive south along the beach.
properties.comments: Caution should be taken over driving vehicles on the beach other than over the low tide period.

landing.landing_description: Landing zone is on the beach in front of takeoff and is large, especially at low tide.

properties.name: Castle Rock
properties.takeoff_description: 1km West of the Mt Cavendish Gondola.
properties.flight_rules: 3500 feet maximum altitude unless air traffic control has been contacted.
properties.going_there: Land early if any sign of sea breeze coming in.
properties.weather: Do not fly in NW winds. Landing area can become turbulent if the the sea breeze comes in.

properties.name: Tangihua
properties.flight_rules: Within MBZ 171

properties.name: Muriwai
properties.comments:
Please be careful. There is sacred Maori land that must be respected, and also some of the neighbours don't like people flying too close to their houses.  When the wind is coming from a particular direction, things can also get very turbulent.  I personally know of 2 broken backs at this site, and almost killed myself here twice too (by being an idiot). This site is deceptively calm-looking.

Please talk to the contacts listed before flying here - they're real friendly. ;)

properties.name: Mt Cheeseman
properties.takeoff_description: Drive up the Mt Cheeseman ski field road to the locked gate, then walk a few hundred meters to the ski field base station.
properties.flight_rules: Max altitude 9500 feet, right under the flight path for incoming flights to Christchurch International.

properties.name: Glover Park (G-spot)
properties.takeoff_description: Demanding Cliff launch suitable for experienced pilots. Difficult top landing behind tree line in compression zone and through rotor
properties.flight_rules: Heli Vector lane either side.
properties.going_there: Drive to the end of Waitara road, St Helliers.
properties.comments: Fantastic soaring site very close to the city. Close to cafes and amazing views over the city. Sun sets behind city skyline.
properties.weather: Takes N to ENE. Because of cliff launch can be difficult to takeoff when strong and if wind increases getting blown back is very hazardous.

properties.name: Piha North
properties.takeoff_description: Cliff site on private site
properties.going_there: Drive to Piha north carpark. Walk up Anawhata track to top
properties.comments: This is a private site and important you contact local pilots before going there. Very difficult to describe how to find the property and property owner must be called prior
properties.weather: Only takes S. SW will have rotor on the takeoff.

properties.name: Puketutu
properties.takeoff_description:
TEMPORARILY CLOSED FOR LAMBING.  Enter with permission, but animals not to be disturbed.

Access to the NW launch ( and a short walk around to the NE launch) can be gained by following the signs to Mt William walkway at the end of Puketutu Rd.
properties.flight_rules: This site is located in GAA G275 with a height restriction of 4,500ft ASL. The area just north of Puketutu is GAA G276 with a height restriction of 3,500ft ASL but able to be opened to 4,500ft ASL by notifying ATC. Refer to comments in the front of this guide under heading of airspace.
properties.going_there: Puketutu is located on the Bombay Hills, south of Auckland. Take the southern motorway to Bombay, turn left at Bombay exit off the motorway, left, right and onto road signposted to Paparata. Take the second on the right then the first turning left into Main Road. Access to the site is on the right several hundred metres down Main Road through a farm gate.

properties.name: Karioitahi A
properties.takeoff_description: The 'High Site' also known as 'The Main Cliff', 300 m north of the access road. (Used by PGs when wind is too light for the other launch sites).
properties.flight_rules: These sites are located within the outer area of CTA/C with a height restriction of 2,500 foot A.S.L, reducing to 1,500 foot approximately 8km north of Karioitahi, and over the township of Waiuku behind and to the east of Karioitahi
properties.going_there: From the car park, walk  north on the Beach, cross the stream, the concealed track is 20 m right hand.
properties.comments: Be aware of being caught behind ridges when the wind is off to either the South of the North.

landing.landing_description: When landing on the beach keep look out for beach traffic particularly through summer and when the tide is high. There is a 'no landing zone' that extends roughly 50 m north and south of the grassy derigging area in front of the bottom carpark. Please do your best to avoid landing close to the grassy derigging area when there are lots of other beach users about. Keep an eye out for vehicles and hoons on bikes before setting up for a landing.

properties.name: Karioitahi E
properties.takeoff_description: The top take-off located at the top of the cliff.(This is the main Karioitahi HG launch site.)
properties.flight_rules: These sites are located within the outer area of CTA/C with a height restriction of 2,500 foot A.S.L, reducing to 1,500 foot approximately 8km north of Karioitahi, and over the township of Waiuku behind and to the east of Karioitahi
properties.going_there: This sites is accessed by either leaving the vehicle outside the Lifesavers Club, walking along the beach and up the cliff (PG) or, alternatively taking the private road from beyond the restaurant (PG & HG).
properties.comments: It is unwise to use the top take-off (site E) in a southerly (wind very cross anyway) as there is no escape if your launch is not perfect or you are in risk of being dragged side ways. Be aware of being caught behind ridges when the wind is off to either the South of the North.

landing.landing_description: When landing on the beach keep look out for beach traffic particularly through summer and when the tide is high. There is a 'no landing zone' that extends roughly 50 m north and south of the grassy derigging area in front of the bottom carpark. Please do your best to avoid landing close to the grassy derigging area when there are lots of other beach users about. Keep an eye out for vehicles and hoons on bikes before setting up for a landing.

properties.name: Port Waikato
properties.takeoff_description:
On arrival at Sunset Beach there is a grassed area to the left of the toilet block and, on the southern side of this grassed area a private driveway access and little bridge across a small creek. Pass beyond the small bridge and you will find the obscure beginnings of the track which runs up through toitoi bushes and along the ridge heading south from the beach.

Hang gliders have previously used a launch located a short way along this track. This small launch area is on the edge of the cliff and is unsuitable for paragliders. The second top takeoff point is further up the same track where it exits the bush onto a large rounded hilltop.

On strong days it is also possible to launch from the sand dunes immediately in front of the cliffs to the left of the carpark and beach entrance area.
properties.flight_rules: This site is located just within the boundary of CTA/C with a height restriction of 2,500 feet.
properties.going_there: This site is located on the West Coast on the southern side of the Waikato River. Take the motorway south from Auckland to the Bombay Hills, follow the signposts to Tuakau, and from there the signposts to Port Waikato and Sunset Beach.
properties.comments: Take care when soaring in the bowl to the south of the top takeoff as switches in wind direction can result in one or other side of this bowl being in rotor.

properties.name: Coronet Peak
properties.takeoff_description:
SUMMER time, carpark #4 or rocky gully, or hike to top of mt. wind mostly S.

WINTER time, top of mt either green gates or back saddle. wind mostly N, but sometimes S
properties.flight_rules:
500ft above top of mt. from W big rock on rd on the way up. to S the main rd.(malaghans) to E start of Arrowtown. Check VFR at take offs orweb site. Must be member of NZHGPA, landing fees apply.
All about NZ airspace: http://www.nzairspace.appspot.com/
properties.going_there: driving from Queenstown to Arrowtown on Malaghans to coronet peak rd 'corner' 16kms,then 8kms from main rd.'malaghans rd' to ski resort.
properties.comments: summer time it works W/S/E wind. North not so good. visit www.nzhgpa.org.nz to get club advise. DO NOT FLY OVER HOUSES ON THE VALLEY.
properties.weather: North W North E strong rotor.

landing.landing_description:
Flight Park. 3.3kms from main take off, carpark #4 800meters diff.
See picture for 'no-fly zone'

properties.name: Van Ash
properties.takeoff_description: On the side of the road leading to Taylors Mistake take off.
properties.flight_rules: Max 3500 ft AGL
properties.comments:
Permission required from Van Asch Deaf Education College to land in school grounds during school day.

Light thermal site.
properties.weather: Do not fly NW or NE 10km+

landing.landing_description: Van Ash School

properties.name: Cass Bay
properties.takeoff_description: 400 meters east of the Castle Rock car park on the Summit Road.
properties.going_there: You can get the gondola then take the track west to the Bridle Path, then a further 300 meters west to the south facing take off.
properties.weather: Best flying is in light or dropping S to SW winds. Wind speed can increase rapidly here but this is easily seen on the water of Lyttleton harbour. If the wind is W of SW expect significant turbulence. Do not fly in NW winds.

landing.landing_description: Bottom landing is in the sports ground in Lyttleton. Top landing is possible but care is required due to the rocky ground.

properties.name: Britten Reserve
properties.takeoff_description: 500 meters East of the gondola on the Summit Road.
properties.flight_rules: Maximum altitude 3500 feet.
properties.going_there: Drive up Mt Pleasant road to the top then turn right and drive a further 200 meters, takeoff is on the right over the style.
properties.comments: Contact local pilots before flying from this site. Nice light W wind soaring site often flown in the winter months.
properties.weather: Do not fly in NW winds. Ensure that wind is not SW by driving to Bridle path first.

landing.landing_description: Heathcote sports ground. Do not land there if cricket is being played.

properties.name: Scarborough Cliffs
properties.takeoff_description: Take the road to Taylors Mistake beach from Sumner, look for the track down to the left about 400 meters from the high point of the road.
properties.flight_rules: Maximum altitude 3500 feet.
properties.comments: This is a PG3 rated site for good reason, you must get a site briefing before flying here.
properties.weather: Take-off can be turbulent if wind is N. If E wind picks up pilot can get trapped at the N end.

properties.name: Kourarau
properties.comments: Before visiting pilots fly any WHGPC sites please contact a club member - go to website: http://whgpc.org.nz/

properties.name: Paekakariki Hill
properties.comments: Before visiting pilots fly any WHGPC sites please contact a club member - go to website: http://whgpc.org.nz/

properties.name: Takaka Hill
properties.takeoff_description:
Approx 960m
Faces SW
Be aware of 2 sets power lines. One crossing from saddle to valley the other a single wire from antennas on summit.
properties.flight_rules: Site info available on T/O
properties.going_there: 1H 15 from central Nelson at top of Takaka Hill.   At end of top overtaking lane just before descent turn right with care onto gravel road.  Continue approx 2 k to obvious airstrip on right.  Park next to fence.  Take Off is on west side of road.
properties.weather:
Be aware of sea breeze coming over from eastern side and southerlies from over the back.
In summer the valley breeze can be strong.
Be aware of small planes crossing over and using saddle road as reference.

landing.landing_description:
On field in valley near corner of road.
Field doubles as airstrip and has top dressing shed at northern end.
Tell tails at northern end.

properties.name: Mt Murchison
properties.takeoff_description:
At summit of Mt Murchison.
approx 1450 metres
properties.going_there:
2 hours from central Nelson.
Requires 4x4 vehicle.
Requires multiple permissions from landowners.
Best done through organised group with local club.

properties.name: Barnicoat
properties.takeoff_description: Very sensitive site due to proximity of airport.  The control tower MUST be contacted by phone (035470799 ext 9)before take off.  Obtain briefing from loclal club ( http://www.thgpc.org.nz/ ) or from local pilot.
properties.flight_rules:
Max 500 feet AGL and limits north and south.
Contact Control Tower (035479799 ext 9)before taking off.
properties.going_there:
Go with a local pilot or school.
Obtain on site briefing.
properties.comments: Did we mention the sensitive nature of this site.  Get a briefing from a club pilot and don't spoil it for the locals.
properties.weather:
Don't fly in winds east of north.
Be aware of strengthening sea breeze in summer.
Watch for signs of SW winds.

landing.landing_description: If landing at Octopus Park lose height IMMEDIATELY after crossing power lines. (airport now even closer than at takeoff).

properties.name: Mt Climie
properties.comments: Before visiting pilots fly any WHGPC sites please contact a club member - go to website: http://whgpc.org.nz/

properties.name: Dalefield Rd ( Mt Dick )
properties.comments: Before visiting pilots fly any WHGPC sites please contact a club member - go to website: http://whgpc.org.nz/

properties.name: Ohope
properties.takeoff_description:
This site is largely abandoned due to the actions of the hostile property manager.

There is also the matter of the large step in the front face causing all sorts of substantial rotor in the launch area.  

If you can get airborne from the public lookout or some other way, then go for it, but otherwise enter onto this property at your peril.
properties.comments: Almost all pilots, and sometimes their wives as well have been angrily dressed down by the property manager.

landing.landing_description: Don't top land this site, unless you can get into the public lookout.  Use the beach.

properties.name: Kohe Point
properties.takeoff_description:
Launch area is a little scruffy, steep, and restricted in size.  

No overrun, due trees immediately below launch - requires enough wind to lift you off your feet and a firm run or you will be treed right on the edge of the cliff!  Zero-wind launches are out of the question.  Minimum wind 10km/hr approx, or at pilots' discretion.
properties.flight_rules: This site is below the Instrument Approach to NZWK RWY 27.  Maintain 1000ft vertical and 1 NM horizontal separation from cloud.  Maintain a good outlook for traffic when above 1000FT.
properties.going_there: You need two vehicles for this site, as it's a substantial walk back to the top, and top-landings at the carpark are too dangerous.
properties.comments: Absolutely NO DOGS.  This is a KIWI ZONE.
properties.weather: The LZ next to the marae can be turbulent.

landing.landing_description:
Land on the reserve next to the Whakatane river right in front of launch - better options available toward the south of the reserve.  

No top land available at carpark due severe turbulence, despite large grassy area.  Top land at launch for smartass gurus only - put your name here if you can do it.  ;)

properties.name: Skyline Gondola
properties.flight_rules:
DO NOT FLY AT THIS SITE WITHOUT A NZ LICENCE/MEMBERSHIP OF THE NZHGPA, WITHOUT A PAGER, WITHOUT BEING LOGGED INTO THE WEBSITE, WITHOUT KNOWING THE GAA SITE BOUNDARIES AND WITHOUT BEING ACCREDITED.
THERE ARE SERIOUS CONSEQUENCES FOR ANYONE WHO DOES!
All about NZ airspace: http://www.nzairspace.appspot.com/

properties.name: Bird's Clearing
properties.takeoff_description: Requires permission for access from landowner.
properties.comments:
Contact Local Club for further information:
http://www.thgpc.org.nz
or local School:
Nelson Paragliding

landing.landing_description: Pohara Beach

properties.name: Pukerua Bay escarpment
properties.takeoff_description: Please contact a member of the Wellington Hang Gliding and Paragliding Club BEFORE flying at this site!  http://www.paraglidingearth.com/pgearth/index.php?club=1080
properties.comments: Before visiting pilots fly any WHGPC sites please contact a club member - go to website: http://whgpc.org.nz/

properties.name: Maketu
properties.takeoff_description: Flat area right on the edge of the ridge.
properties.flight_rules: Nil, but caution the low-level VFR traffic between NZWK and NZTG.
properties.comments:
You MUST telephone the owner before arriving.  Barry 07 5332298.  DO NOT turn up unannounced! 

This is a nice ol' couples lovely back yard, so be cool. ;)

Park ON THE ROAD WELL CLEAR of any driveway entrance.  You may drive a load of gear to the top of the driveway, unload it, and then PARK THE CAR ON THE ROAD!

The owners' house is at the top of the long driveway, on the left.  His name is Barry.
properties.weather: Lots of rotor on lifting your wing, and a sharp lift/rotor spike 50 meters to your right after launch.

landing.landing_description:
Top land - caution the rotor when the wind is straight in.  

Cross-wind landing on the beach below and to the south.  Limited or no beach area for landing to the north.

properties.name: Mount Maunganui
properties.takeoff_description:
Assorted flat area for takeoff and top-land.
See flight regulations below BEFORE takeoff.
properties.flight_rules:
This site is in the Tauranga CTR/D.  YOU MUST CALL THE CONTROL TOWER at the airport and ask to activate G271.  Tower: 118.3 123.4 129.2

YOU MUST NOT CLIMB above 1500FT QNH or you will breach the Tauranga CTR/D airspace above.  Calibrate your vario at beach level, or else get the QNH from the ATIS 126.6
properties.going_there: Stiff 40 minutes walk from the car park below.

landing.landing_description: Top land, or easy landing on the large sandy beach near Marine Parade.  Caution the substantial number of beach-goers during the high season in December to February, and one other fine weekends.

properties.name: Hamurana
properties.takeoff_description:
Te Waerenga Road / Hoko Road Airstrip - Unknown and UNFLOWN Development Site.
Would a SO or PG3 please check this ridge out.
properties.flight_rules:
NZRO Airport 5NM SE. Tower 121.2  ATIS 128.8  

Rotorua Lakes Aerodrome - Expect low level Floatplanes.
properties.going_there: North side of Lake Rotorua.
properties.comments:
Possibly a good winter flying site - directly into the prevailing southerly breeze.
Senior pilot to comment, or fly and document this please.
properties.weather:
There is no wind meter nearby that can be used for this site.  If you know of a nearby weather station, ask its' owner to broadcast to the MADIS or windfinder sites, and then that data will appear here automatically.
Alternatively, if you live locally, then consider donating a windmeter to someone near the LZ.

landing.landing_description: Unknown and UNFLOWN Development landing area

properties.name: SnowPark
properties.takeoff_description: On the right side of the car park

landing.landing_description: On the left off the road

properties.name: Raglan
properties.takeoff_description: Easy takeoff from reserve adjacent carpark.
properties.going_there: 5 minutes from Raglan.

landing.landing_description: Large sandy beach below, or spacious top-landing area.

properties.name: Bobs Hill
properties.takeoff_description: Lots of space on the top of the ridge for takeoff.
properties.going_there: Private property!  Ask at the old farmhouse with the orange roof.

landing.landing_description:
Loads of space for an easy top land, or bomb-out north of the road.

Before you leave the roadside, very carefully choose your landing zone on the north side of the road.  Overhead power wires are nearly invisible from the air, and here there's LOTS of them!

properties.name: Rogers Road
properties.takeoff_description: Selection of low-level sand dunes to play on.  Varies 5-20 meters Alt.
properties.going_there: Public Land.
properties.comments: Good for when the higher sites are blown out.

landing.landing_description: Anywhere on the beach or grassy reserve.

properties.name: Turangi Road
properties.takeoff_description:
Unknown and unflown Development Site.

20-30M cliffs NE-facing in this area.
properties.flight_rules:
Site is inside NZNP CTR/D. Pilots to contact NZNP Tower and advise ATIS version, QNH, position, intentions, request clearance to enter, before Flying. 


http://www.aip.net.nz/pdf/NZNP_35.1_35.2.pdf

Site is abeam D322 Danger Area. 

Very close to the instrument let-down area for NZNP RWY 23. Maintain VFR clearance vertically and horizontally from cloud at all times. 

NZNP ATIS 127.05 
NZNP Tower 124.7 125.4
properties.comments:
Unknown and unflown development site.

SO or PG3 to comment.

properties.name: Urenui
properties.takeoff_description:
This is not a site.  This is a reference to this whole sea-side area - NW to WNW facing 20-200M cliffs for many km to the North, MIGHT support some really epic soaring trips, possibly 50km the way up to Mokau or futher!

Unflown and unresearched.  SO or PG3 or higher to fly and document.
properties.flight_rules: Just clear on NZNP CTR/D to the north.  Remain well clear of cloud, and expect light aircraft to be hugging the coastline.
properties.weather: Could be anything!

landing.landing_description: Cannot recommend any landing locations.  SO or PG3 to determine.

properties.name: Ohiwa Hill (Onekawa Pa)
properties.takeoff_description:
Take-off from the flat top of the Pa site or, if the wind is strong, a little lower on the hill facing NW. Take-off direction should always be towards Whale Island (the closest island you can see in NW direction) to avoid tall trees. Do not take off towards the fence and trees in a straight-north direction (big chance of sinking into the tall Pohutekawas after takeoff).

Best place to lay-out your glider is on the very back (S) ridge of the site, as far towards the west as possible. Airflow is cleanest there and take-off easiest.

To get your bearings on this site; White Island (Whakaari) is straight north. This is the puffing active volcano about 50 km off the coast. On some hazy days you can't see it, but it's pretty much straight out to the ocean (90 degrees on the beach). Anything left of White Island is more towards the west, anything right of White Island is more towards the east (and if the wind is coming from there the site is not flyable, see "Weather" below).

Whale Island (Moutohora) is directly NW. Anything to the right of Whale Island is more towards the North, anything left of Whale Island is more towards the West. The end of Kohe Point ridge is WNW (and if the wind is coming from there it gets very turbulent, see "Weather" below).
properties.flight_rules: Absolutely no push-bikes or motor-bikes up the walking tracks. Vehicle access is not allowed without prior permission from DOC. Other than that the campground owners appreciate it if you stick your head into their reception office to let them know you will be flying the hill. Permission is always granted; it's just a common courtesy to let them know you will be flying above their campground and landing (or packing) your wing on their campground. The entire hill is owned by DOC and operated as an active farm, so please leave gates as you find them. There are no access restrictions during lambing season, but please don't cause any trouble so we can keep it this way.
properties.going_there: 40 minutes east of Whakatane, 20 minutes west of Opotiki. Take exit "Onekawa Pa" off SH-2. Take a left over the bridge and up the hill. At the bottom of the hill, take a right onto Ohiwa Harbour Road. The first house you see on the right (with the windsock on the harbour edge) belongs to some friendly local pilots. Always welcome to stop by for info. Continue driving until you see the entrance of the Ohiwa Harbour Campground on the left. Park your car on the grassy area across the road from the entrance (next to the 50 speed sign) and walk to the reception office. Let the owners know your intentions, then walk past the barriers and enter the path up the hill on your right. Follow the path until you hit a T. Take a left, walk a bit further and go through the gate. After the gate immediately right, steep up the hill. Keep following this path until you reach the take-off. The entire hill is owned by DOC and operated as an active farm, so please leave gates as you find them.
properties.weather:
The site is good in a NNW-N. North gets very difficult to take-off, but once in front if will be super buoyant.

In NW it is recommended to not fly past the little spur towards the east (and into the bowl facing north). In a NW It gets very turbulent on the western side of the bowl, and if you get low you'll have to fight into wind to get on the windward side of the hill again.

When it gets more W (WNW or W), the hill still looks like it is flyable, but in fact isn't. You'll notice very quickly if you take-off anyway; turbulent in front of the hill with very little lift.

As soon as there is a bit of E component, it gets almost impossible to take-off. There is no take-off possibility towards the NE at all. Even if you are able to take-off towards the NW in these conditions, you will fly straight into a big turbulent, rotory sink hole. You'd have to fly through all that around the corner towards the east to find marginal lift. Not worth it.

The prevailing wind in summer is NW-NNW due to the seabreezes. The seabreeze usually starts every sunny day between 10 and 11 AM, and stops about 30 minutes to an hour before sunset. BEWARE of a sudden wind direction change when the seabreeze stops: It is not uncommon to have a nice 12 knot NNW seabreeze turn into a nasty 22 kts southerly within minutes! You will feel it coming (starts to get turbulent, less lift, wind-lines on the ocean disappear or change direction suddenly), but it's safer to just be on the ground well before sunset.

It is very important to know how to read wind-lines on the ocean so you can determine the true wind direction. Because this is a steep hill with a flat top, the hill will "feel" flyable in most wind directions. Make sure you know the true wind-direction before you takeoff.

When in doubt; stop by the local pilots that live in the two story house at nr 240 on the road towards the campground (you'll see the windsock on the harbour side). They will be able to tell you if the conditions are good or not.

landing.landing_description:
Normal landing area is between the tall Norfolk Pine and the beach. You can land anywhere in the dunes or further out on the beach. The dune area is not flat, so take care.

Take extra care in high season (December-February) when the campground is full. Always land with ample clearance of any tents, caravans, trees, and people. Remember; not everybody thinks we are in full control, so just stay away to avoid any misunderstandings.

When in doubt, land on the beach. It's only a 150 meter walk back to the campground where you can pack your wing on the grass.

Top landing is possible, but for expert pilots only:

When the wind direction is N - NNW; fly to the very end of the ridge, towards the swimming pool. Turn and fly towards the back ridge of the take-off (your approach to the take-off is from the west). If too low (at any time); bail out and fly to the front of the hill to try again. If too high, make figure-8 turns above the back (S) ridge of the take-off until you are low enough to top-land into wind. Turbulence in this wind direction is minimal, as long as you don't go too far back (never cross the fence that runs along the walking path south of the take-off)

When the wind is coming more from the WNW - NW; from the spur (just before the bowl), fly straight out towards the ocean. Keep looking back towards the hill and turn back until you are at the right height to fly over the highest tree on the ridge with a meter or so (your approach to the take-off is from the NE). Once you are over the tree on the ridge, it will get quite turbulent for a bit until you connect with the back of the take-off. If you are too high (you normally are); make figure-8's until you are low enough to land into wind on the top. 

This latter option is the more turbulent route, but you can't come in from the west anymore because you will be flying with the wind towards the take-off at too high speed to make a safe top-landing.

properties.comments:
WARNING: Franz Joseph is THE BUSIEST Heliport in the southern hemisphere. DO NOT FLY unless you follow the rules below. 
Fly above the glacier if there is no wind but beware of the catabatic wind (down the glacier).
Best is to climb in the afternoon, try to fly in the evening after the helicopters have finished or camp overnight up there and take off in the morning. You must have an airband radio on the helicopter frequency.
properties.weather: beware of the catabatic wind (down the glacier).

properties.takeoff_description: Please always call at the farm house before proceeding, site owners Mark and Poppy Keskic are very friendly. The takeoff at the top of the hill is 900 foot A.S.L. properties.flight_rules: This site is located on the edge of CTA with a height restriction of 3,500 feet A.S.L immediately above launch, until you pass a line to the north running between Five Fingers and Dills Hill when the restriction rises to 4,500 foot A.S.L. properties.going_there: This site is located 8 kilometres West of Dills Hill on West Coast Rd that runs from Araparere to Woodcocks. Quickest access is up state highway 16 past Kaukapakapa. properties.name: Duders Peninsular
properties.takeoff_description:
Take-off height at the northerly site is 280 foot A.S.L, normally in front of the trig, although the bowl immediately to right can be used also.
HG vehicles to be kept to a minimum. Drive slowly up the track towards the Trig. Park before the trig. DO NOT DRIVE PAST THE TRIG because the road there is subsiding and there are serious OSH issues involved. In other words, there is vehicle access to the northerly site, but you have to park before you come to the trig.   
When the wind is square in (northerly) the whole Peninsula can be flown, if it is off to the north west or north east it will be marginal going around to and back from the eastern end. Take-off heights at the south easterly site is 180 foot A.S.L, adjacent to the top dressing fertiliser bins. The best top landing is also in this area so vehicles should be parked as close as practical to the bins.
properties.flight_rules: This site is located within CTA/C with a flight ceiling of 1,500 feet, and the south easterly site is located within low flying area number L261 so be aware of other aircraft below Ridge height and close to the hill.
properties.going_there:
https://www.google.co.nz/maps/place/Duder+Regional+Park/@-36.913186,175.0653363,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m2!3m1!1s0x6d72b71ef8712c11:0x77ccd850d3bae1e5

The Duders Peninsula (both north and south eastern sites) is now all a ARC park and access permission should be obtained first by referral to Paul the ranger on mobile 021 676 300 or site monitor as detailed below and private and business phone numbers. Permission should be confirmed from the ranger before taking any vehicles into the park and only the minimum number of vehicles should be taken. Arrange to go in convoy, the balance of vehicles being left in the parking area before passing through the padlocked gate. The ranger is particularly concerned over pilots flying on their own. The rules do not permit this anyway but please respect this request or we are likely to lose the privilege of flying here.
properties.comments: Owing to the gentle contours of the south easterly site it is mainly soarable in stronger winds and often there is a fine line between the site being soarable and becoming too strong. For paragliders the North site is rated PG2 but the South East site is rated PG2 plus 30 hours. For hang gliders both sites are rated Intermediate.
